programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Tha cuileag anns an t-sadhbhaidh agus tha Fuigheag dha ruaig. Cha chuir càil stad air oir cha bhi Fuigheag na thàmh ach nuair a bhios e na chadal! There’s a fly in the den and Fuigheag is in pursuit. Nothing will stop him - Fuigheag is never still unless he’s sleeping!

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: Tha Linda NicLeòid a’ còcaireachd cuide ri a caraidean. An-diugh tha Cara agus Calvin ga cuideachadh a’ dèanamh mìlseag bhlasta le rùbarab. Ach mus tòisich iad, feumaidh iad a bhith cinnteach gu bheil na stuthan a tha a dhìth orra a-staigh. Mur a bheil, bidh iad a’ dèanamh liosta agus a’ dol dhan bhùth airson a h-uile càil fhaighinn. Bidh Linda agus a caraidean cuideachd a’ faighinn a-mach cò às a tha siùcar a’ tighinn. Tha iad an uairsin a’ tilleadh dhan chidsin airson a’ mhìlseag a dhèanamh mus suidh iad sìos aig a’ bhòrd ga ithe. Linda Macleod is joined by Cara and Calvin to make a delicious rhubarb pudding. Before they start, they have to ensure they have all the ingredients. If not, they make a list and go shopping. They also learn more about where sugar comes from and then it’s back to the kitchen to make the rhubarb pudding, before sitting down to tuck in.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha solas na gealaich cho àraid is cho àlainn is gu bheil e doirbh cadal. Tha Tilidh a’ co-dhùnadh Àtaidh a thoirt a-mach air chuairt airson a dhèanamh sgìth. Ach chan fhada gus a bheil i fhèin a’ faireachdainn uabhasach sgìth is tòrr aca ri fhaicinn fhathast. The moonlight is so strange and beautiful that it's hard to sleep. Teal decides to tire Abney out with an adventure, but she is soon feeling sleepy herself, and there is still a lot to look at.

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha daolag-bhreac is Seillean ’g ionnsachadh mun fhaid a leumas fionnan-feòir. Ladybird and Bee discover how far a grasshopper can hop.

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Beach shoes have gone missing and red hair is found at the scene - Grumblestunk is blaming Stan! Who really did it? Dan and Gran spy a mystery! Tha brògan traghad air a dhol a dhìth; tha falt ruadh ga lorg aig an làraich 's tha Greannarlobht a' coireachadh Dan! Ach cò tha cionntach? Tha rùn-dìomhair ro Dan is Gran!

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Joy Dunlop a’ leughadh Finn is na Breugan Beaga. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh is a dhealbhachadh le Hugh Percival agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Màiri NicCumhais. A bedtime story for young children. Joy Dunlop reads Finn is na Breugan Beaga, written and illustrated by Hugh Percival and translated into Gaelic by Mairi MacCuish.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Aig àm-cadail tha Pòl ag ithe cèic-càise a chaidh a dhèanamh dhan chàraid. Tha e an uair sin ga lorg fhèin steigte ann an aisling chàise le theaghlach, is tha e ag ionnsachadh nach fhaigh e às mura h-aidich e na rinn e agus mura cuir e aghaidh ri chiont càise. Bedtime, and Dave has eaten a cheesecake that was not meant for him. Finding himself stuck inside a cheesy dream with the rest of the Spuds, Dave discovers that the only way to escape is to admit what he has done and confront his cheesy guilt.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Anna agus Pòl a’ togail dèideag slaodaire bho phìosan a th’ air an toirt seachad an-asgaidh ann am bogsaichean de ghràinean bracaist. Ach nuair a tha an dèideag a’ fas nas motha na bloca nam flataichean aca, feumaidh iad dòigh a lorg airson an t-slaodaire mhòir a chumail fo smachd. Anna and Dave are building a toy sloth from the parts given away free with every Bran Cran Krustee cereal box. But when their toy ends up bigger than Grimsby Heights, Dave and Anna must find a way to keep it under control.

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Nuair tha Twig air teicheadh, tha Hilda is a màthair a' dol ga lorg. Tha iad den bheachd g’ eil e a’ caoidh an fhàsaich is tha seo a’ toirt cianalas orra-san cuideachd – gach cnoc, gach coille, an t-saorsa. Ciamar a gheibh iad air adhart? When Twig runs away, Hilda and her mum go in search of him. They think he is missing the wilderness and this also makes them feel nostalgic for the hills, forests and the freedom. How will they get on?

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra
programme.desc: Mairi Rodgers explores Kailzie Gardens near Peebles. Tha Màiri Rodgers a’ gabhail cuairt tro Ghàrraidhean Kailzie faisg air na Pùballan.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Joy Dunlop gar toirt tro na h-ath cheumannan gus Gàidhlig a bhruidhinn. Tha Iain MacGillÌosa à Uibhist a Tuath a’ bruidhinn ri Joy agus tha Calum MacIlleathain le saill mu bhilean is e an tòir air càise air Taobh Sear Rois. Joy Dunlop guides us through the next steps to speak Gaelic. North Uist native and learner John Gillies chats to Joy, and a hungry Calum Maclean is on a quest for a mouthwatering cheese course at a family dairy in Easter Ross. Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne aig www.speakgaelic.scot agus ann an sreath phodcastan air BBC Sounds. Supporting materials can be found online at www.speakgaelic.scot and in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Suas gu Deas
programme.desc: Tha croitearan Uibhist a’ cruinneachadh airson a’ chiad fhèill uain den bhliadhna ann a Loch na Madadh, tha Ruairidh is Peter a’ dol a-mach a dh’iasgach agus tha Mòd Loch Abar a’ teannadh dlùth dha Còisir Ghàidhlig Bharraigh agus Sgioba Dràma Uibhist. Uist crofters bring their best lambs to the first sale of the year in Lochmaddy, while Ruairidh and Peter go out sea fishing. Mod week is fast approaching for Barra Gaelic choir and the Uist drama group as they get ready to compete. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Cocain is na Klondykers
programme.desc: Sreath aithriseach mu iomairt dhrogaichean cho mòr ’s a bha a-riamh ann an eachdraidh Alba. Documentary series investigating one of the biggest drug seizures in Scottish history.

programme.title: Cùram
programme.desc: How illness or injury can lead to a person having sudden or unexpected care needs.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Mary Ann and Lucy hunt the 'good for you' plants and those that definitely aren’t.

programme.title: Machair

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Fàilte gu Fraochy Bay , baile nach fhaic thu a h-uile là! Is iomadh annas a tha ri fhaicinn sa bhaile , agus sin gun ghuth air cail ach muinntir a bhaile fhèin. Tha a chlann a' toirt caraid mor gu fear nam fiaclan. Welcome to the colourful and unusual world of Fraochy Bay, a miniature metropolis somewhere off the fringes of the map. Local schoolchildren present the dentist with a monstrous problem.

Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gives some top tips on how to protect your home when you’re away. And Matt also hears from a teenage hero whose camera captured the moment he rescued an elderly lady from a burning building.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin sees the warning signs directly spelt out to him at a Merseyside property. Jacqui meets four friends in Suffolk embarking on their first property project. And Dion is in Yorkshire, where he wants to fill a void.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp is in her home city of Glasgow, where she visits the world-famous Burrell Collection – 9,000 rare antiques and artworks that were donated to the city in 1944. Meanwhile, Danny Sebastian and Roo Irvine are on hand to help the reds and the blues.

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: The drugs unit arrest a man on cruise ship in a major bust, there's a mystery, a missing phone at the golf course, and the police are on hand to assist at a tourist bike crash.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson joins up with Sheli McCoy, aka Gladiator Sabre, to explore her home area of Fife. They take a paddleboard tour of the coast, followed by a farm stay overnight. In the morning, they embark on a stunning road trip to Ansruther, where they take a boat trip to the nature reserve of the Isle of May. Famous for its bird life, fauna and flora, the pair attempt to capture the scene with landscape artist Liz Myhill.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Jules Hudson is in Powys, helping Lisa from Northampton achieve a life reboot. With a budget of £450,000, she wants a fresh start in the Welsh countryside for her and her two children. There’s an exciting mix of homes on offer, including a 17th-century mystery mansion... or at least a wing of it. On a break from the property shopping, Jules takes things to new heights as he canoes across the breathtaking Pontcysyllte Aqueduct, paddling a dizzying 128 feet above the ground.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris and Flo are in Winchester to transform Stefan and Lucinda’s unloved plot into a garden where they can indulge their love of making meals outdoors. They would love a kitchen in the garden and a spot to grow produce they can cook on the barbecue. Can the team achieve all this on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Phoebe, Katie, Sam and Cal – take on the Bridge of Lies. programme.title: Bridge of Lies

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Phoebe, Katie, Sam and Cal – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: Matt Allwright hears from Ann, who woke up to find she’d been robbed while she was asleep, but other doorbell detectives hold the crucial evidence to bring them to justice. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gives some top tips on how to protect your home when you’re away. And Matt also hears from a teenage hero whose camera captured the moment he rescued an elderly lady from a burning building.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin sees the warning signs directly spelt out to him at a Merseyside property. Jacqui meets four friends in Suffolk embarking on their first property project. And Dion is in Yorkshire, where he wants to fill a void.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp is in her home city of Glasgow, where she visits the world-famous Burrell Collection – 9,000 rare antiques and artworks that were donated to the city in 1944. Meanwhile, Danny Sebastian and Roo Irvine are on hand to help the reds and the blues.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: The drugs unit arrest a man on cruise ship in a major bust, there's a mystery, a missing phone at the golf course, and the police are on hand to assist at a tourist bike crash.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson joins up with Sheli McCoy, aka Gladiator Sabre, to explore her home area of Fife. They take a paddleboard tour of the coast, followed by a farm stay overnight. In the morning, they embark on a stunning road trip to Ansruther, where they take a boat trip to the nature reserve of the Isle of May. Famous for its bird life, fauna and flora, the pair attempt to capture the scene with landscape artist Liz Myhill.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Jules Hudson is in Powys, helping Lisa from Northampton achieve a life reboot. With a budget of £450,000, she wants a fresh start in the Welsh countryside for her and her two children. There’s an exciting mix of homes on offer, including a 17th-century mystery mansion... or at least a wing of it. On a break from the property shopping, Jules takes things to new heights as he canoes across the breathtaking Pontcysyllte Aqueduct, paddling a dizzying 128 feet above the ground.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris and Flo are in Winchester to transform Stefan and Lucinda’s unloved plot into a garden where they can indulge their love of making meals outdoors. They would love a kitchen in the garden and a spot to grow produce they can cook on the barbecue. Can the team achieve all this on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Phoebe, Katie, Sam and Cal – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Ria Lina for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: BBC News at Six
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.desc: The latest news, sport, weather and features from the South East of England.

programme.title: EastEnders

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: The two finalists head to Longleat Estate to transform rental cottages, taking inspiration from either the nearby safari park or from the surrounding countryside. They aim to show judges Michelle Ogundehin and Laurence Llewelyn-Bowen how much their design ability has evolved during the competition before one of them wins Interior Design Masters and a partnership with retailer Next for their own homewares range.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson joins up with Sheli McCoy, aka Gladiator Sabre, to explore her home area of Fife. They take a paddleboard tour of the coast, followed by a farm stay overnight. In the morning, they embark on a stunning road trip to Ansruther, where they take a boat trip to the nature reserve of the Isle of May. Famous for its bird life, fauna and flora, the pair attempt to capture the scene with landscape artist Liz Myhill.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Jules Hudson is in Powys, helping Lisa from Northampton achieve a life reboot. With a budget of £450,000, she wants a fresh start in the Welsh countryside for her and her two children. There’s an exciting mix of homes on offer, including a 17th-century mystery mansion... or at least a wing of it. On a break from the property shopping, Jules takes things to new heights as he canoes across the breathtaking Pontcysyllte Aqueduct, paddling a dizzying 128 feet above the ground.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris and Flo are in Winchester to transform Stefan and Lucinda’s unloved plot into a garden where they can indulge their love of making meals outdoors. They would love a kitchen in the garden and a spot to grow produce they can cook on the barbecue. Can the team achieve all this on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Phoebe, Katie, Sam and Cal – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: At Hillhead farm, John and Antoinette have their hands full, as Ben’s had to take a full-time job away from the farm. In Fife, the Morrises head into lambing season, expecting nearly 900 lambs. But unseasonably cold and wet weather causes devastating results. On Hawkhill croft, Sally and dad Iain are vaccinating their ewes, and Sally takes her mum out of hospital for a birthday lunch.

programme.title: Reported Missing
programme.desc: Police mount urgent searches for two teens missing from care: a 13-year-old who has failed to return after school, and a risk-taking 18-year-old who has not been seen for five days.

programme.title: Murder Case
programme.desc: In 1984, 58-year-old Mary McLaughlin was found dead in her home in Glasgow. She had been strangled with the tie of her dressing gown. Mary was last seen walking home from the pub at night, with an unknown man following her. Despite the best efforts of the investigating officers, they couldn’t identify the unknown man and the trail would run cold for decades. In 2014, advances in DNA profiling gives new hope to cold cases. Police Scotland detectives and forensic scientists reinvestigate the case, sampling items preserved from the original crime scene to try and find Mary’s killer. A DNA hit leads to a potential suspect, but even more questions arise when this person appears to have an ironclad alibi. The case won’t be solved by forensic science alone, and detectives need to go back to basics and hunt in the archives for clues to figure out who killed Mary. In this documentary, we hear from both the original 1984 investigators as well as contemporary Police Scotland detectives and forensics team who cracked the case.

programme.title: High
programme.desc: Michaella describes the dilemma she faced: stick to her story about being forced to carry the drugs and face 15 years in jail, or come clean and break her mother’s heart.

programme.title: High
programme.desc: Despite being sentenced to nearly seven years in a maximum security prison, Michaella was home in less than three. She reveals how she got out and how prison changed her for the better.

programme.title: Brickies
programme.desc: The brickies are back in Northampton for the second week on a new affordable housing development. With the Euro football championships underway, excitement on site is growing about the biggest match of the tournament so far: England versus Germany. The brickies have planned a big night out to watch the game. In the meantime, Molly realises her career aspirations will only be reached if she can overcome her fear of driving. Apprentice Lucas experiences some on-site struggles. When brickies’ foreman Jack catches up with him, shared personal revelations put everything into perspective. The night of the England match comes, and the brickies go large, but they pay for it the next morning. With the news of a site inspection from the boss, their hangovers are put to the test. The mood is helped when Molly returns with a big surprise from the local newsagent.

programme.title: Brickies
programme.desc: The brickies head to a village in Derbyshire, where a retaining wall is needed to protect a housing development from possible land slips and flooding. Multi-talented Lauren is drafted in to help give things a push, but she isn’t impressed by some of the attitudes on site. With dreams of becoming a property millionaire, Lauren is keen to gain skills in bricklaying. Lucas experiences setbacks on and off-site as he confesses that his relationship is on the rocks. After struggling to get to grips with a new method of bricklaying, he pulls on the boxing gloves and enjoys sparring with Lauren. Jeorgia is happy to have her dad working alongside her, but when an anticipated delivery of bricks fails to materialise, production on-site is at risk of stalling. Labourer Tom C believes he can save the day with an ingenious solution - one that only he can provide.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Animation. It’s 1995, and welcome to Dave’s Games: your one-stop shop for all things video games, from computers and consoles to poppers and Pogs - and how can you forget the floor-to-ceiling piles of plastic game cartridges? Self-appointed ‘gaming legend’, shop owner and father (in that order), Dave is the king of his own crumbling kingdom. Sure, there is mould on the ceiling and some of the oldest video games you’ve ever seen (even for 1995), but it’s the only games shop in town. At least until the gigantic, shiny, futuristic rival shop Turbo Gamez opens just down the road. And they also happen to be releasing the newest and most sophisticated piece of gaming technology the world has ever seen: the first PlayStation…

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall heads to a place very few people ever go: Snake Island in Brazil, where the concentration of snakes is higher than anywhere else on earth.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall goes in search of one of Europe’s most venomous snakes: the nose-horned viper. He also hopes to track down a bear and goes deep into a cave system to find a dragon.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May attempt to find a trio of cars which are equally at home on the racetrack as they are transporting a family to the shops, for a budget of £5,000. They end up with a BMW M3, a Mercedes 190E and a Ford Sierra Cosworth, which they put through their paces in Europe's home of speed, Germany. James also makes a rare visit to the Top Gear track to test a pair of Porsches - the 911 Sport Classic and Boxster Spyder - and Alastair Campbell is the star in the all-new reasonably priced car.

programme.title: Louis Theroux
programme.desc: Louis Theroux is in America to interview members of the Church of Scientology - but they do not want to speak with him. So he meets disaffected former members of the controversial organisation and uncomfortably recreates some extreme experiences. All the while, Louis is being oddly shadowed by people who might be the very folk he wouldn't mind having a word with...

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May test the Aston Martin Rapide, the Porsche Panamera Turbo and the Maserati Quattroporte as they attempt to find the world's greatest four-seat supercar. After an early morning start in the City of London, the boys embark on a road trip across the south of England, stop off for a race around a closed-off business park, and end up undertaking a rather special chauffeuring job. Meanwhile, Richard is on the test track in two very different muscle cars, the Chevrolet Camaro SS and Mercedes E63 AMG. And there's a double dose of celebrity as Harry Potter star Rupert Grint and F1 ace Rubens Barrichello take their turns as the Stars in a Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: Charlie Cooper’s Myth Country
programme.desc: Charlie Cooper, who wrote and starred in the BBC’s This Country, has a fascination for the weird and wonderful world of British folklore. In this episode, with the help of an old AA van, he goes in search of Black Shuck, the demon dog of East Anglia. Despite a local legend that seeing Shuck brings with it a curse, Charlie meets locals who claim they have survived such encounters. Keen to capture the beast on camera, he attempts an overnight stakeout, with unexpected consequences. Alleged sightings of this 900-year-old hell hound are recorded almost monthly, so is Charlie in with a chance? His humorous odyssey takes him across Norfolk and Suffolk, where he meets witnesses and learns that in Britain almost every county has its own mythical creature. You only need to scratch the surface anywhere in this land to discover that folklore, myth and legend are very much alive.

programme.title: Charlie Cooper’s Myth Country
programme.desc: Charlie Cooper’s odyssey takes him to Wiltshire, home to ancient sites such as Stonehenge, Avebury and the Westbury chalk horse. He wants to get to the bottom of why humans feel the need to leave marks on the landscape. He soon turns his investigation towards a far more recent phenomenon, crop circles, hoping to settle a debate that has plagued his family for years. They believe that crop circles are the work of aliens, but Charlie strongly doubts that. He meets with farmers and secretive 'croppies' (humans who create crop circles), trying to find out how these vast and intricate shapes appear overnight. Helped by his friend Scott, Charlie takes his research one step further and attempts to shed light on the phenomenon by making his very own crop circle. The humorous trip aboard an old AA van shows him that you only need to scratch the surface anywhere in this land to discover that folklore, myth and legend are very much alive and exert a beguiling power.

programme.title: Charlie Cooper’s Myth Country
programme.desc: Charlie Cooper has always loved the stories of King Arthur, especially the ones about his buried treasures. He digs out his metal detector, says goodbye to his family and embarks on an Arthurian investigation. He travels to Wales, the land of dragons and song, on a mission to discover if King Arthur was a real man or just a myth and if there’s any truth behind this treasure story. In the process, he meets treasure hunters of different sorts, a recorder of rare and ancient folk songs, and finds what he refers to as 'his tribe', a metal-detecting club from South Wales. He’s optimistic he will return home a rich man - if not in wealth, then certainly in knowledge.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Adam Henson are in Lisburn, Northern Ireland, for the Balmoral Show, the region’s largest agricultural and food event, welcoming more than 100,000 visitors each year. As the show celebrates its 157th year, Sean and Adam meet the people who make it such a vital gathering for the region’s farming community and explore how events like this are crucial to their future. Adam explores heritage crafts that community members are determined to preserve, and he joins families showing their prize livestock. Sean takes charge of the stopwatch at the tractor-handling competition and gets hands-on with traditional local produce that is valuable to the region’s economy.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham, Michaela Strachan and the team are live from the National Trust's Crom Estate as nature writes its own stories, with triumph, heartbreak and surprise around every corner. The live remote cameras are capturing fledging, predation and drama around the clock, from otters on the lough shore to red squirrels in ancient woodland. Meanwhile, Iolo Williams remains at the Knepp rewilding estate in Sussex, where he takes a look the lives of some of the country's rarest species.

programme.title: Cher Meets Rylan
programme.desc: The goddess of pop sits down for a fun and in-depth chat with Rylan Clark about her new record, biggest hits, and incredible life and career. Featuring archive footage from across the decades of Cher's hit records and television appearances, illustrating her glittering music career, success in film, iconic fashion choices and the ways she has influenced so many people.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Can you guess the answer to David Harper’s question at the start of the show? You’ll have to watch for more clues! While David bamboozles fairgoers in Detling with his mystery item, two best friends take on a team of twins in a bid to make the most money at auction and win the coveted golden gavel. In red are pals Roo and Yas, who met while playing tennis at school, but can they ace their opponents, twin brothers Ben and Luke? The lads admit to having different tastes, but they always manage to compromise. With expert Mark Stacey by their side, the reds take a shine to a vintage-looking desk lamp, but it doesn’t have the age they’re searching for. Meanwhile, the blues brothers and Kate Bliss hit the ground running – literally – skidding to a stop by a stall selling two giant wooden seahorses. Is it neigh or yay to the sculptures or, more importantly, from the bidders at today’s saleroom in Windsor?

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris and Diarmuid are in Oxford to help Adam, Vaneesha and her father, Graham, transform their two triangular, mirror-image gardens each with a patio and a solitary shed into one vibrant, family-friendly space. In memory of Vaneesha’s late mother, the garden will be bursting with colourful flowers celebrating her Indian heritage. It will also serve as a sensory haven for their autistic daughter, Raveena, with features like water play and a Wendy house for imaginative fun. While designed to be low maintenance, Graham hopes to enjoy some flowers of his own. Vaneesha and Adam, who live next door to Graham with their three daughters, want a peaceful garden where the whole family can come together, play and find comfort in each other’s company. Can the team unite these two awkward plots into one stunning garden on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Northern Ireland, a devastating wildfire tears through the Glens of Antrim, threatening farmland, homes and livestock. As flames spread across the hills, the fire service battle to save buildings, animals and livelihoods. With a drone team and the Irish Air Corps called in, it becomes a race against time to stop the blaze before it consumes everything in its path. In North Yorkshire, police close in on a brutal gang of badger baiters, after a tip-off from a local Rural Watch group leads officers to a car full of suspects and a horrific crime scene. As forensic evidence is pieced together, investigators are determined to bring the perpetrators to justice. And in Hertfordshire, reporter Paul Colgan experiences the challenges of rural policing first hand when he gets behind the wheel of a 4x4 to navigate rough terrain and uncover the realities of crime in Britain’s countryside.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The detectorists climb the fells at Crummock Water in blistering heat, hoping to find a bracelet given to a heartbroken daughter by her late father. The freedivers are out in force, searching Ullswater for a precious pendent, and jeweller Nisha turns old damaged coins into treasure again.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Queen's Tennis
programme.desc: Live coverage from day 2 of the 2026 Queen's tennis tournament.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Simon Armitage, Josie Gibson, Ardal O'Hanlon and Adele Roberts take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Ably assisted by Lila, an expert labrador, Michael Portillo hunts for truffles in the Istrian countryside near the hilltop town of Buzet. His railway adventure through the Balkan countries of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina then continues on the fashionable tourist coast at Opatija, which he reaches in style in the driver’s cab of a brand new electric train. In Rijeka, Michael discovers the history of a bizarre military coup led by an Italian poet in the aftermath of the First World War. He finishes on the moonscape island of Pag, where he helps to make the salty cheese for which the island is famed.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: Marcus is visiting a local farmers' market, where each week a local French chef impresses the crowds with a live cooking demo. However, he’s been told a British chef is cooking tonight, and that chef… is Marcus. Can he convince the locals that Brits know how to cook? Later, Marcus has a VIP guest coming for dinner, the mayor of St Remy’s sister, and he really wants to impress. As she is a bit of a history buff, he decides to do some research into the origins of some local produce to find culinary inspiration.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan broadcast live from National Trust Crom in Northern Ireland, where the nests they’ve been watching for weeks are bursting at the seams with fledging chicks. Who will stay and who will go? Iolo Williams is experiencing the captivating cacophony resonating from the seabird colonies at Bempton, on the spectacular Yorkshire coast, plus more celebrations of the wonderful cast of British wildlife up and down the country.

programme.title: QI XL
programme.desc: Sandi Toksvig hosts a specially spooky episode of QI with David Mitchell, Richard Osman, Zoe Lyons and Alan Davies.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: Chris McCausland welcomes comedians Sophie Duker and Emmanuel Sonubi to the stage.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Brexit: A Very British Civil War
programme.desc: As David Cameron wins a shock majority at the 2015 general election, the implications immediately dawn on all concerned. There is no coalition negotiation to stop the Conservatives from fulfilling an election pledge to hold a referendum on whether Britain should leave the EU. Nigel Farage fails to win a seat and resigns as UKIP leader but quickly U-turns. He sets up Leave.EU to campaign for Brexit. Meanwhile, as Cameron continues his negotiation with the EU, his demands are watered down. It makes it even more important he recruits Boris Johnson and Michael Gove to the Remain campaign - but they haven't yet made a decision.

programme.title: Ali & Ava
programme.desc: Devoted mother and grandmother Ava, a teaching assistant with a love of country and folk music, is offered a lift home from school by the charismatic Ali, who is estranged from his wife but continuing with the charade of marital domesticity for the sake of their close-knit relatives in Bradford. On the journey, they find many things in common, including a love of music, and begin an unusual and secretive courtship.

programme.title: Brexit: A Very British Civil War
programme.desc: As David Cameron wins a shock majority at the 2015 general election, the implications immediately dawn on all concerned. There is no coalition negotiation to stop the Conservatives from fulfilling an election pledge to hold a referendum on whether Britain should leave the EU. Nigel Farage fails to win a seat and resigns as UKIP leader but quickly U-turns. He sets up Leave.EU to campaign for Brexit. Meanwhile, as Cameron continues his negotiation with the EU, his demands are watered down. It makes it even more important he recruits Boris Johnson and Michael Gove to the Remain campaign - but they haven't yet made a decision.

On the journey, they find many things in common, including a love of music, and begin an unusual and secretive courtship.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Adam Henson are in Lisburn, Northern Ireland, for the Balmoral Show, the region’s largest agricultural and food event, welcoming more than 100,000 visitors each year. As the show celebrates its 157th year, Sean and Adam meet the people who make it such a vital gathering for the region’s farming community and explore how events like this are crucial to their future. Adam explores heritage crafts that community members are determined to preserve, and he joins families showing their prize livestock. Sean takes charge of the stopwatch at the tractor-handling competition and gets hands-on with traditional local produce that is valuable to the region’s economy.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham, Michaela Strachan and the team are live from the National Trust's Crom Estate as nature writes its own stories, with triumph, heartbreak and surprise around every corner. The live remote cameras are capturing fledging, predation and drama around the clock, from otters on the lough shore to red squirrels in ancient woodland. Meanwhile, Iolo Williams remains at the Knepp rewilding estate in Sussex, where he takes a look the lives of some of the country's rarest species.

programme.title: Cher Meets Rylan
programme.desc: The goddess of pop sits down for a fun and in-depth chat with Rylan Clark about her new record, biggest hits, and incredible life and career. Featuring archive footage from across the decades of Cher's hit records and television appearances, illustrating her glittering music career, success in film, iconic fashion choices and the ways she has influenced so many people.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Can you guess the answer to David Harper’s question at the start of the show? You’ll have to watch for more clues! While David bamboozles fairgoers in Detling with his mystery item, two best friends take on a team of twins in a bid to make the most money at auction and win the coveted golden gavel. In red are pals Roo and Yas, who met while playing tennis at school, but can they ace their opponents, twin brothers Ben and Luke? The lads admit to having different tastes, but they always manage to compromise. With expert Mark Stacey by their side, the reds take a shine to a vintage-looking desk lamp, but it doesn’t have the age they’re searching for. Meanwhile, the blues brothers and Kate Bliss hit the ground running – literally – skidding to a stop by a stall selling two giant wooden seahorses. Is it neigh or yay to the sculptures or, more importantly, from the bidders at today’s saleroom in Windsor?

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris and Diarmuid are in Oxford to help Adam, Vaneesha and her father, Graham, transform their two triangular, mirror-image gardens each with a patio and a solitary shed into one vibrant, family-friendly space. In memory of Vaneesha’s late mother, the garden will be bursting with colourful flowers celebrating her Indian heritage. It will also serve as a sensory haven for their autistic daughter, Raveena, with features like water play and a Wendy house for imaginative fun. While designed to be low maintenance, Graham hopes to enjoy some flowers of his own. Vaneesha and Adam, who live next door to Graham with their three daughters, want a peaceful garden where the whole family can come together, play and find comfort in each other’s company. Can the team unite these two awkward plots into one stunning garden on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Northern Ireland, a devastating wildfire tears through the Glens of Antrim, threatening farmland, homes and livestock. As flames spread across the hills, the fire service battle to save buildings, animals and livelihoods. With a drone team and the Irish Air Corps called in, it becomes a race against time to stop the blaze before it consumes everything in its path. In North Yorkshire, police close in on a brutal gang of badger baiters, after a tip-off from a local Rural Watch group leads officers to a car full of suspects and a horrific crime scene. As forensic evidence is pieced together, investigators are determined to bring the perpetrators to justice. And in Hertfordshire, reporter Paul Colgan experiences the challenges of rural policing first hand when he gets behind the wheel of a 4x4 to navigate rough terrain and uncover the realities of crime in Britain’s countryside.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The detectorists climb the fells at Crummock Water in blistering heat, hoping to find a bracelet given to a heartbroken daughter by her late father. The freedivers are out in force, searching Ullswater for a precious pendent, and jeweller Nisha turns old damaged coins into treasure again.

programme.title: My Life
programme.desc: With Women’s Rugby World Cup fever riding high, one rising star has her eyes set on the top. Talented, fearless and utterly dedicated, 14-year-old Ava is used to pushing herself hard - but this summer, something unexpected shifts. Her coach asks her to help with a younger girls’ team who are at risk of dropping out, and Ava starts to see how much rugby can give beyond winning. Along the way, she meets her Red Roses heroes, watches them play in the World Cup opener and pushes herself to the limit at her first England trials. What begins as a summer about chasing her own dream soon becomes a powerful journey of connection, confidence and discovery. As Ava helps inspire others to stay in the game, she realises what rugby truly gives you - and why lifting others can matter as much as any trophy.

Supertato and Carrot try to stop her in the Tatocar, but Evil Pea ices the floor and gets away using the Evil Peamobile's skis. It’s Carrot's job to add more gadgets to the Tatocar. They head out on their brand new skis - but Evil Pea starts shooting snowballs from her Peamobile and corners the Tatocar! Luckily, Carrot has another new gadget ready. The Tatocar turns into the Tatocopter and dodges the snowballs, which causes them to fall back on Evil Pea.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and his friends are making leaf pictures in the woods. They take a piece of paper, place it on a leaf and rub a crayon onto it. They each choose their own leaf, but Bing's is whisked away by the wind! Luckily, he manages to catch it by stamping on it. When the wind also whisks Coco's picture off the table, Bing tries to catch it but once again ends up stamping on it. Now Coco is angry!

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Preston’s automated scooter tour of Swoppiton doesn’t go as planned. Mojo and Bo must find a way to chase down and scoop up those scooters, and get the tour back on track!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Snake tells Slug to hurry up and join him for a new Squirrel Club adventure, Norrie counts shells on a beach, then it's time for a game! Finally, learn a skipping song with the Squirrels. Eugene teaches everyone how to create a song.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Happy notices a tiny fruit fly on his apple, and the Squirrels are amazed by how small it is. The fly tells them that there are things even smaller than him, and so Duggee teaches them that some things are so small that you can’t even see them – atoms. Combined, these make molecules, which in turn join to make cells, the fabric that makes up every living thing. The Squirrels discover that things can be wide, long, thin or small, and that these attributes make up all sorts of different sizes. To help understand this, they assign a line-up all the way from a small piece of dust to a huge rocket ship.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bingo pretends to be Bluey’s new employee in the middle of Dad’s backyard workout!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey is playing circus with her friends but Hercules wants to play his game instead.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: The Go Jetters are adventure-seeking explorers who soar around the planet fixing environmental problems caused by Grandmaster Glitch!

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: Benjamin's up in the air as the unwilling passenger of a flyaway kite! Can Peter and Lily put aside their differences and work together to rescue their friend?

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. The Octonauts use magnets to try to stop a meteor that's heading toward the Octopod and get an assist from a rock-chomping humphead parrotfish and her friends.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Uh-oh. Unlucky Thirteen falls apart whenever anyone mentions his name. Learn all about the number 13 with Numberblock Thirteen!

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. P, A, R, T and Y need some help getting the party started! S tries her best, but they really need someone extraordinary to liven things up and superhero Exciting X soon gets the party popping with his special powers.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Brinicle invites his Piri friends round to taste his brilliant brioche. Yuk - it’s chewy and hasn't risen at all! Despite this, Brinicle announces he has entered a baking competition. A disaster looms, but Flutter has an idea.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Bella and Lift have fun playing with paper plates, just like Sketch in Boxtropolis, who makes paper plate mega monster masks.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Sula and Amma have come to Bing's house for lunch but there are no carrots, so Flop pops to the shop to get some. Bing stays behind but it's not long before he starts to miss Flop. Missing Flop... it's a Bing thing!

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘swing’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We see all sorts of swings – a red swing, a black swing, a forward and back swing. There’s a tyre swing, a basket swing, a flower swing and even a rainbow swing! Not to mention, King Banana on his brilliant banana swing.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Lu struggles to do all the things she wants to do in her new costume.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Lou has a series of misadventures whilst fast asleep, so Kiri exhausts herself trying to keep him safe.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: With a bit of Froggie help, Pipp turns into a queen with a crown, a throne and a royal parade.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are on a beach, where they watch a couple of children building a sandcastle. When the children run away to join their parents, the Twirlywoos come out and start to add more sand to the sandcastle. They get carried away and build a huge sandcastle, which towers over the kids and their parents when they return. Peekaboo brings a strange jelly out of the hole in the wall which gets bigger each time someone touches it. When the Twirlywoos return to the boat, they investigate, and cause the jelly to get so big that it fills the entire boat!

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Ben meets Maliah and Betsy at the park, where they have fun in the playground and listen for sounds that are loud and quiet. Grandad Tumble is having a nap, and Mr Tumble tries not to make too much noise. There's musical fun in the spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words playground, grass and loud.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Po eats Tubby Custard and gets a messy bib. Po washes the bib clean and hangs it out to dry before eating more Tubby Custard with Tinky Winky, Dipsy and Laa-Laa.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Roman, Rosa-May, Inam, Theo Joseph, George, Tobias and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are toothbrushes which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding safe, baby appropriate toothbrushes inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun song ‘Let’s Give Our Teeth a Brush’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children create rainbow art, learn British Sign Language signs for red, rainbow and pink, then sing and sign the colourful song, I Can Sing a Rainbow.

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: World-renowned botanist Chris introduces the Fact Pack to the Venus flytrap. They discover how this incredible plant catches its prey, including a very special trick it plays in the dark! They also find out about other extraordinary carnivorous plants.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: A new zebra arrives at the orphanage and everyone is very excited! Hamza meets some incredible giraffes in the wild and joins the elephants as they find somewhere nice to graze.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: A Mandarinteryx has moved into home base and is causing a big mess.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey's having fun copying everything Dad says and does, but the game takes a serious turn when Bluey finds a hurt budgie and they have to make an emergency trip to the vet.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels have made a song. They enjoy playing for others but wish they had a chance to see how they perform together. Duggee explains that they can if they make a music video, which tells a story. There is a lot to prepare beforehand, such as lights, costumes and glitter, and as they prepare, we are immersed into Enid’s dream, where she gives a star performance in her own eclectic music video! The Squirrels are taught to practice their dance moves before filming, to pick the perfect location and to try and put something unexpected into the video. After lots of collaboration, creativity and fun, the Squirrels finally get to watch their own music video and are thrilled at the results.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Cool Blue arrives in Colourland. Learn about the colour blue

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Woody finds out all about superhero spiders! Ferne meets a tarantula and feeds a wolf spider at the zoo, while Rory and his son Sandy go on a spider safari in the garden and at the park. Plus, we find out how spiders are amazing predators that are great for the environment.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: George and Freddie love having fun! After a hearty breakfast, they fill their day with family 'eggsperiments', art, and even set up an obstacle course for Mum and Dad to complete. It looks easy at first… until they learn they have to do it blindfolded!

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Holly comes from the English city, Liverpool. She will be making two tasty recipes. The first is a local Merseyside stew called scouse, made with chopped and cooked carrots, potatoes and onions with gravy, cooked beef, bay leaves and her special ingredient: celery. The second is a side of crusty bread. Holly makes a dough and stirs in yoghurt and honey. Then it is topped with more yoghurt and pumpkin seeds and placed in the oven. Holly also serves pickled beetroot and cabbage, a traditional side to scouse. Will Holly's friends enjoy her delicious food, and will they enjoy the celery once it is cooked in her recipe?

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Maddie is at the coast! She visits a red and white striped lighthouse and meets the lighthouse keeper right at the top. She goes inside to where the bulb is kept and finds out how all the reflective glass that surrounds it helps make the light stronger. Then she uses a special drone camera that flies out to sea! The drone camera shows us how strong the light bulb is because it needs to warn ships miles out to sea that there's shallow water or rocks nearby. Next, Maddie visits a factory where bath bombs are made to find out about the ingredients that make bath bombs fizz! She discovers why it’s called a chemical reaction. Maddie uses her special underwater camera to show us the fizzy bubbles that are made when the bath bomb is dropped into water.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: It’s Mum’s birthday, and Rayane is preparing an extra-special secret birthday surprise. He’s baking a cake, painting a teapot and borrowing some bunting from Sally next door to decorate the house.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet a lesser hedgehog tenrec. This tiny and very cute character is covered in spines, just like a hedgehog, but these amazing animals live on the island of Madagascar. Next, they meet Kate the tarantula. As Lizzie holds her, Aneeshwar discovers that Kate is covered in small hairs. This spider is super furry. These two animals are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Baba has a new friend... now, where did he go?

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: TapTap’s loud, fast drumming is driving everyone in the garden to distraction. Can Yukee and Twinkle find a way to show TapTap that fast doesn’t necessarily have to mean loud?

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs get the giggles as they repeatedly ask Dad 'are we there yet?' during a family car journey to Nana and Dadó's. If only Dad hadn't tried to take a shortcut!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Chipmunk is cycling one day delivering his packages when he hits a rock and his trike falls apart! He has so many packages to deliver - what is he going to do now? Duggee offers to repair Delivery Chipmunk’s trike, but that will take too long. The packages need to be delivered right away or else! Duggee also has a delivery badge and he will try to deliver all of Chipmunk’s packages with the help of the Squirrels. Before they begin, they need to learn the rules of delivering. With some hard work, the Squirrels deliver all the packages and Delivery Chipmunk is alright again. The Squirrels have truly earned their delivery badge!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: One explores the Double Dungeon of Doom in search of the golden apples, doubling herself all the way up to Octoblock. Learn how to double and halve numbers up to 8 with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. J wants to sing and fly like a bird - can A and friends help?

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Mr Tumble gets messy decorating a cake. Maddie meets Alfie and Jack for a day out, and they play games and create paintings. There's some face painting fun in the spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words ball, colour and paint.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po watch bunny rabbits. Bunny ears and tails appear on the Teletubbies. They do the bunny hop hop before saying 'eh oh' to the Tiddlytubbies.

programme.title: Andy's Dinosaur Adventures
programme.desc: Andy travels back in time 152 million years, to the era of diplodocus - a massive 25-metre-long plant-eating dinosaur. His mission is to find and pick a giant fern to replace the one he accidentally broke back at the museum. Along the way he witnesses an adult diplodocus knocking down trees with its front legs. Will he succeed before the museum opens?

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: When a rogue ball destroys Mr Parks’s competition-ready bug hotel, Evie, Taran and Jaz help him rebuild it using a combination of football skills and teamwork.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: Series for young children that celebrates lots of different amazing machines. In this episode, motorcycle rider Grace shows off three amazing food machines! Grace drives an incredible solar-powered ice cream van and shows off a hi-tech delivery robot. Then, she delivers some milk in a milk float!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: George and Freddie pretend to be pirates and head to a nearby boating lake. But will they find any treasure?

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: The Octonauts guide migrating monarch butterflies on a journey south for the winter.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When the rabbits are forced out of their secret treehouse, they learn that finding a new hideout isn't the hard part... it's keeping it secret!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are excited to learn that Mr Wobbly, the jelly juggler, is coming to town, and they can’t wait to see him. But they become impatient, so Duggee makes sure to explain to them that the week will fly by and there’s a lot to be done in that time. Duggee explains that a week is made up of seven days and what activities he does each day to stay busy. Each squirrel excitedly shares their usual plans between Monday and Friday so that they have something to look forward to while they wait for Mr Wobbly’s arrival.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Sunny wants to win a box car race but doesn’t feel like his team is taking it seriously.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Evil Pea tricks Supertato into believing that he has no superpowers without his red cape. When he rescues his friends without it, he discovers that he has superpowers - cape or no cape!

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings get creative and make sculptures of themselves out of straw. Weasy thinks he can do better, but his sculpture is a fiasco. The Farm of the Future offers a precise cutting system. Will Weasy be able to outsmart his daughters?

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Mojo and Bo need to move a crashed meteor. But every time Mojo goes near the big rock, moving turns to grooving. How can you move a meteor if you can’t stop dancing?

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bingo pretends to be Bluey’s new employee in the middle of Dad’s backyard workout!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey is playing circus with her friends but Hercules wants to play his game instead.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: The doctors realise Fergus's bog mud has healing properties. Fergus starts to feel overwhelmed when they send everyone to the bog for treatment.

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: When Jen’s drone goes missing on Dino Island, Andy heads out on an epic adventure to track it down. He discovers one of the island’s inhabitants, a giraffe-sized pterosaur called Hatzegopteryx, is using the drone for a very special purpose. Along the way, he meets a herd of stampeding triceratops.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Evie pretends to be Waffle’s dog friend. She even wears a headband with doggy ears. Waffle loves it when they play together like this but Simon calls Evie for school - it is time to leave. Evie says her goodbyes together with Simon and Doug and she promises she will play with Waffle again later, when she returns home. Waffle is disappointed that his playmate has left but Jess cheers him up - she suggests they play doggy chase before she goes to work. Jess puts on doggy ears and chases Waffle on all fours into the bedroom where Jess’s mobile phone rings. It is Angela from the kennels, calling with news of a sad dog she wants Jess to examine. Jess assures Angela she will come right away and invites Waffle to join her. Waffle is very excited and when he arrives at the kennels with Jess, he still wants to play chase.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi wants her dads to stop doing chores and to dance with her. She wishes to be the oldest so that she can set the rules. Suddenly, Jake and Dash turn into babies, leaving Rafi in charge! It’s funny at first, but soon the mess grows. Rafi realises being a grown-up means taking responsibility. She cleverly mixes tidying with dancing, showing them chores can be fun too. When the wish ends, her dads return to normal and are proud of Rafi’s maturity and teamwork.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran take a trip to have JoJo’s eyes tested at the opticians. Jaxon and Ezra help explain what it means to be long- and short-sighted. After his eye test, Jaxon is struggling to decide which glasses he would like to wear. JoJo really wanted to pick new glasses too, but she doesn’t need them. Gran Gran has a plan: JoJo can help Jaxon pick his new glasses! Back home, JoJo makes Panda some glasses.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Scarf Lady takes to the skies in a knitted hot air balloon to race against an old sporting friend.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: A space dustcart drops a lot of rubbish on the Clangers’ planet. The Clangers notice that one of these bits looks surprisingly like a robot. Major Clanger tries to get it to work, and to his astonishment, he succeeds. The robot comes to life, and even more amazingly it seems able to speak in Clanger-ese, although in a voice different from the Clangers’ whistle. The Clangers soon discover that this is a household helper robot. But sometimes helpfulness can be too much of a good thing.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa dress up as a happy clown, a superhero, a tiger and in silly glasses. At the Play Tree, BaBa and MeMo excitedly choose a pretty tutu to play with, but BaBa is sad when it doesn’t fit. It fits MeMo perfectly. When MeMo shrinks down for Yummy Time, MeMo feels sad that the tutu no longer fits and understands how BaBa must be feeling. MeMo finds a way for them to both play with the tutu.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: The Tombliboos discover the game of waving. They wave to everybody as they fly through the garden in the Pinky Ponk. Even the great big Haahoos wave back. The Tombliboo waving game makes everyone in the garden happy.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Singer and Celebrity Traitor Cat Burns reads the tale of a little fib that grows and grows

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s the speedy dancing Runner Beans, who won’t stand still for even one minute.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing inadvertently pees on his blankie during his bedtime routine, and it's too wet to wash and dry before bed. Fortunately, his Hoppity Voosh toy has a cape just as soft and huggy as blankie, and it even smells just right too.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: As the Teletubbies say eh-oh to their reflections in a puddle, Dipsy's hat falls in and gets wet - oops! Dipsy sings a sad song, but then the sun shines and the wind blows, and his hat is dry again in no time! In Tummy Tales, the Teletubbies watch children enjoying their reflections in a Scottish loch.

programme.desc: A Mandarinteryx has moved into home base and is causing a big mess.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey's having fun copying everything Dad says and does, but the game takes a serious turn when Bluey finds a hurt budgie and they have to make an emergency trip to the vet.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels have made a song. They enjoy playing for others but wish they had a chance to see how they perform together. Duggee explains that they can if they make a music video, which tells a story. There is a lot to prepare beforehand, such as lights, costumes and glitter, and as they prepare, we are immersed into Enid’s dream, where she gives a star performance in her own eclectic music video! The Squirrels are taught to practice their dance moves before filming, to pick the perfect location and to try and put something unexpected into the video. After lots of collaboration, creativity and fun, the Squirrels finally get to watch their own music video and are thrilled at the results.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Cool Blue arrives in Colourland. Learn about the colour blue

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Woody finds out all about superhero spiders! Ferne meets a tarantula and feeds a wolf spider at the zoo, while Rory and his son Sandy go on a spider safari in the garden and at the park. Plus, we find out how spiders are amazing predators that are great for the environment.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: George and Freddie love having fun! After a hearty breakfast, they fill their day with family 'eggsperiments', art, and even set up an obstacle course for Mum and Dad to complete. It looks easy at first… until they learn they have to do it blindfolded!

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Holly comes from the English city, Liverpool. She will be making two tasty recipes. The first is a local Merseyside stew called scouse, made with chopped and cooked carrots, potatoes and onions with gravy, cooked beef, bay leaves and her special ingredient: celery. The second is a side of crusty bread. Holly makes a dough and stirs in yoghurt and honey. Then it is topped with more yoghurt and pumpkin seeds and placed in the oven. Holly also serves pickled beetroot and cabbage, a traditional side to scouse. Will Holly's friends enjoy her delicious food, and will they enjoy the celery once it is cooked in her recipe?

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Maddie is at the coast! She visits a red and white striped lighthouse and meets the lighthouse keeper right at the top. She goes inside to where the bulb is kept and finds out how all the reflective glass that surrounds it helps make the light stronger. Then she uses a special drone camera that flies out to sea! The drone camera shows us how strong the light bulb is because it needs to warn ships miles out to sea that there's shallow water or rocks nearby. Next, Maddie visits a factory where bath bombs are made to find out about the ingredients that make bath bombs fizz! She discovers why it’s called a chemical reaction. Maddie uses her special underwater camera to show us the fizzy bubbles that are made when the bath bomb is dropped into water.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: It’s Mum’s birthday, and Rayane is preparing an extra-special secret birthday surprise. He’s baking a cake, painting a teapot and borrowing some bunting from Sally next door to decorate the house.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet a lesser hedgehog tenrec. This tiny and very cute character is covered in spines, just like a hedgehog, but these amazing animals live on the island of Madagascar. Next, they meet Kate the tarantula. As Lizzie holds her, Aneeshwar discovers that Kate is covered in small hairs. This spider is super furry. These two animals are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Baba has a new friend... now, where did he go?

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: TapTap’s loud, fast drumming is driving everyone in the garden to distraction. Can Yukee and Twinkle find a way to show TapTap that fast doesn’t necessarily have to mean loud?

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs get the giggles as they repeatedly ask Dad 'are we there yet?' during a family car journey to Nana and Dadó's. If only Dad hadn't tried to take a shortcut!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Chipmunk is cycling one day delivering his packages when he hits a rock and his trike falls apart! He has so many packages to deliver - what is he going to do now? Duggee offers to repair Delivery Chipmunk’s trike, but that will take too long. The packages need to be delivered right away or else! Duggee also has a delivery badge and he will try to deliver all of Chipmunk’s packages with the help of the Squirrels. Before they begin, they need to learn the rules of delivering. With some hard work, the Squirrels deliver all the packages and Delivery Chipmunk is alright again. The Squirrels have truly earned their delivery badge!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: One explores the Double Dungeon of Doom in search of the golden apples, doubling herself all the way up to Octoblock. Learn how to double and halve numbers up to 8 with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. J wants to sing and fly like a bird - can A and friends help?

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Mr Tumble gets messy decorating a cake. Maddie meets Alfie and Jack for a day out, and they play games and create paintings. There's some face painting fun in the spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words ball, colour and paint.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po watch bunny rabbits. Bunny ears and tails appear on the Teletubbies. They do the bunny hop hop before saying 'eh oh' to the Tiddlytubbies.

programme.title: Andy's Dinosaur Adventures
programme.desc: Andy travels back in time 152 million years, to the era of diplodocus - a massive 25-metre-long plant-eating dinosaur. His mission is to find and pick a giant fern to replace the one he accidentally broke back at the museum. Along the way he witnesses an adult diplodocus knocking down trees with its front legs. Will he succeed before the museum opens?

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: When a rogue ball destroys Mr Parks’s competition-ready bug hotel, Evie, Taran and Jaz help him rebuild it using a combination of football skills and teamwork.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: Series for young children that celebrates lots of different amazing machines. In this episode, motorcycle rider Grace shows off three amazing food machines! Grace drives an incredible solar-powered ice cream van and shows off a hi-tech delivery robot. Then, she delivers some milk in a milk float!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: George and Freddie pretend to be pirates and head to a nearby boating lake. But will they find any treasure?

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: The Octonauts guide migrating monarch butterflies on a journey south for the winter.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When the rabbits are forced out of their secret treehouse, they learn that finding a new hideout isn't the hard part... it's keeping it secret!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are excited to learn that Mr Wobbly, the jelly juggler, is coming to town, and they can’t wait to see him. But they become impatient, so Duggee makes sure to explain to them that the week will fly by and there’s a lot to be done in that time. Duggee explains that a week is made up of seven days and what activities he does each day to stay busy. Each squirrel excitedly shares their usual plans between Monday and Friday so that they have something to look forward to while they wait for Mr Wobbly’s arrival.

programme.title: Vida the Vet

programme.desc: The ducklings get creative and make sculptures of themselves out of straw. Weasy thinks he can do better, but his sculpture is a fiasco. The Farm of the Future offers a precise cutting system. Will Weasy be able to outsmart his daughters?

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Mojo and Bo need to move a crashed meteor. But every time Mojo goes near the big rock, moving turns to grooving. How can you move a meteor if you can’t stop dancing?

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bingo pretends to be Bluey’s new employee in the middle of Dad’s backyard workout!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey is playing circus with her friends but Hercules wants to play his game instead.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: The doctors realise Fergus's bog mud has healing properties. Fergus starts to feel overwhelmed when they send everyone to the bog for treatment.

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: When Jen’s drone goes missing on Dino Island, Andy heads out on an epic adventure to track it down. He discovers one of the island’s inhabitants, a giraffe-sized pterosaur called Hatzegopteryx, is using the drone for a very special purpose. Along the way, he meets a herd of stampeding triceratops.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Evie pretends to be Waffle’s dog friend. She even wears a headband with doggy ears. Waffle loves it when they play together like this but Simon calls Evie for school - it is time to leave. Evie says her goodbyes together with Simon and Doug and she promises she will play with Waffle again later, when she returns home. Waffle is disappointed that his playmate has left but Jess cheers him up - she suggests they play doggy chase before she goes to work. Jess puts on doggy ears and chases Waffle on all fours into the bedroom where Jess’s mobile phone rings. It is Angela from the kennels, calling with news of a sad dog she wants Jess to examine. Jess assures Angela she will come right away and invites Waffle to join her. Waffle is very excited and when he arrives at the kennels with Jess, he still wants to play chase.

programme.desc: Rafi wants her dads to stop doing chores and to dance with her. She wishes to be the oldest so that she can set the rules. Suddenly, Jake and Dash turn into babies, leaving Rafi in charge! It’s funny at first, but soon the mess grows. Rafi realises being a grown-up means taking responsibility. She cleverly mixes tidying with dancing, showing them chores can be fun too. When the wish ends, her dads return to normal and are proud of Rafi’s maturity and teamwork.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran take a trip to have JoJo’s eyes tested at the opticians. Jaxon and Ezra help explain what it means to be long- and short-sighted. After his eye test, Jaxon is struggling to decide which glasses he would like to wear. JoJo really wanted to pick new glasses too, but she doesn’t need them. Gran Gran has a plan: JoJo can help Jaxon pick his new glasses! Back home, JoJo makes Panda some glasses.

programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Scarf Lady takes to the skies in a knitted hot air balloon to race against an old sporting friend.

programme.desc: A space dustcart drops a lot of rubbish on the Clangers’ planet. The Clangers notice that one of these bits looks surprisingly like a robot. The robot comes to life, and even more amazingly it seems able to speak in Clanger-ese, although in a voice different from the Clangers’ whistle. The Clangers soon discover that this is a household helper robot. But sometimes helpfulness can be too much of a good thing.
